cards.back: Electric potential energy per unit charge at a point.
Charge stored per voltage difference, C=Q/V in a linear capacitor.
At a circuit node, total current entering equals total current leaving.
For a first-order RC circuit, the product RC that sets the exponential response timescale.
The surface integral of magnetic field through an oriented area.
The induced current direction opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it.
The effective impedance seen by a source at an instrument input; finite values can load the source.
An amplifier's ability to suppress voltage shared by both inputs while amplifying their difference.
C_m ≈ 1 μF/cm² = 0.01 F/m²; total C = C_m × area; C = ε₀ε_rA/d.
Q = CV; ions = Q/e, a tiny fraction of the cell's ions.
E = V/d ≈ 10⁷ V/m for 70 mV across 5 nm.
τ = R_mC_m (specific values), independent of cell size.
F = qv × B, magnitude qvB for perpendicular motion; does no work.
ε = B d v across a conducting liquid; independent of conductivity.
ε = −N dΦ/dt; induced current opposes the flux change.
Series R ≥ V_max/I_limit; measure leakage via V across a known resistor with a high-impedance meter.
Sum source fields first; multiply by the signed independent test charge for force.
Scalar potential cancellation does not imply cancellation of its spatial gradient.
Zero net flux can contain nonzero entering and exiting fields.
A spherical outline does not establish a spherically symmetric charge distribution.
Charge, voltage and capacitance must describe the same state when computing stored energy.
Isolated free charge and source-held voltage produce different dielectric-change endpoints.
Source work can supply stored-energy increase, mechanical transfer and dissipation.
Bound charge separation does not require arbitrary added net free charge or ideal conduction.
A new load changes upstream drops; solve all relevant branch currents.
Open-circuit voltage and suppressed-independent-source resistance predict the selected linear port.
Accurate loaded-node reporting still differs from open-circuit source voltage.
A terminal equivalent does not uniquely identify internal currents, temperature or mechanism.
Finite current preserves ideal capacitor voltage at a switch event; retain its initial state.
1−exp(−t/τ) describes completed transition fraction, not always final-voltage fraction.
Source work equals stored-energy change plus resistor heat under the supplied simple model.
A fitted time constant identifies a combination of components; independent constraints separate them.
Use the coordinate convention and charge sign after forming v×B.
Magnetic-only perpendicular motion changes velocity direction while preserving speed.
The magnetic point-force contributes zero instantaneous power; complete circuits can still exchange energy.
Long-wire and solenoid expressions require their declared geometry and steady-current approximations.
Reverse contour and normal together when interpreting signed flux and emf.
The induced effect opposes flux change, which need not mean opposing the existing field.
For the specified resistive bar model, mechanical power equals electrical heat.
Finite voltage preserves ideal inductor current; sustained source work also feeds ongoing resistor heat.
State exp(jωt), amplitude scale and source/input topology before interpreting phase.
Convert sinusoidal peak to RMS before calculating average resistor power.
Parallel input capacitance can cause frequency-dependent loading despite a large DC resistance.
Reporting calibration recovers loaded voltage; source recovery additionally needs the circuit transfer.
A known zero and nonzero node voltage identify a supplied affine reporting offset and gain.
Reporting correction recovers loaded voltage; source/input transfer is still needed for open-circuit recovery.
Parallel input resistance changes both DC gain and the resistance seen by a shared capacitor.
An informative synthetic dummy-source control supports a conditional electrical explanation, not unique real biological identification.
ID=ε0 dΦE/dt; for an ideal charging capacitor, ΦE=Q/ε0 and ID=dQ/dt=I.
The loop circulation of B includes both conduction current and the changing-electric-flux term for the chosen spanning surface.
S=(1/μ0)E×B gives the direction and instantaneous power flux of an electromagnetic field.
For a sinusoidal vacuum wave with peak field E0, ⟨S⟩=(1/2)cε0E0²; use peak-versus-RMS conventions consistently.
For same-frequency waves with no initial source-phase offset, φ=2πδ/λ.
For coherent, in-phase sources: maxima at δ=mλ and minima at δ=(m+1/2)λ.
When L≫d and angles are small, adjacent bright fringes are spaced by Δy≈λL/d.
For two coherent equal-intensity waves, I=4I₀cos²(φ/2); equal amplitudes are needed for fully dark minima.
dB = (μ₀/4π) I dl × r̂/r². Loop on axis: μ₀IR²/[2(R² + z²)^(3/2)], μ₀I/(2R) at the centre. Finite segment: (μ₀I/4πd)(sin θ₂ − sin θ₁).
∮B·dl = μ₀I_enclosed; it gives B only with symmetry. Thick wire inside: μ₀Ir/(2πa²). Toroid: μ₀NI/(2πr). Solenoid: μ₀nI.
F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πd), attractive for currents in the same direction.
μ = NIA along the right-hand normal. Uniform field: zero net force, τ = μ × B, U = −μ·B. Far on the axis, B ≈ μ₀μ/(2πz³).
At ω₀ = 1/√(LC) the reactances cancel, Z = R, and I_peak = V_peak/R; ω₀ and f₀ = ω₀/(2π) depend only on L and C.
Δω = R/L = ω₀/Q; the half-power frequencies straddle ω₀, differ by Δω and multiply to ω₀².
I_RMS = I_peak/√2; average resistor power is I_RMS²R, while ½LI_peak² and ½CV²_C,peak are maxima a quarter-cycle apart.

cards.front: What must be computed before simplifying Gauss law for a nonuniform source?
cards.back: Integrate the declared charge distribution, then use its actual symmetry; the shape of the Gaussian surface alone does not determine the field.

cards.front: Why is the infinite-line potential reference important?
cards.back: Its unshielded logarithmic form cannot simply be assigned zero at infinity. Use the stated grounded boundary and integrate the field relative to it.

cards.front: How can an induced-charge sign be checked independently?
cards.back: Use a Gaussian surface inside the electrostatic metal, whose field is zero, and require the enclosed free/induced charge sum to vanish.

cards.front: Why are two different energy integrals useful?
cards.back: They check different intermediate quantities and boundaries. Agreement is stronger than evaluating one closed expression twice, while still not establishing qualified physics review.

cards.front: Does a negative mutual term prove negative stored energy?
cards.back: No. Check the complete quadratic form and the coefficient bound M²<=L1L2 with the declared current/dot references.

cards.front: What does negative total passive port power mean for a valid inductor state?
cards.back: The stored energy is decreasing and energy is returning through the ports; it does not require a negative stored amount.

cards.front: Why test the full inductance matrix?
cards.back: Passivity is a quadratic-form condition. An isolated cross-term sign or a successful algebraic inverse cannot substitute for that condition.

cards.front: Where does resistive heating energy come from in the steady moving-rod model?
cards.back: The external agent maintaining motion supplies mechanical work against magnetic drag; include that boundary when interpreting motional emf.

cards.front: Why do the two outgoing sheet fluxes add despite opposite vector directions?
cards.back: The outward normals also point in opposite directions, so each outward power contribution is positive.

cards.front: What does a retarded-time argument represent?
cards.back: A field observation depends on the source at an earlier time determined by propagation distance and speed under the stated model.

cards.front: How do electric and magnetic fields combine at an ideal conducting wall?
cards.back: The incident/reflected electric fields cancel tangentially while their magnetic fields reinforce under the declared propagation and reference signs.

cards.front: Can nonzero electromagnetic energy coexist with zero average transport?
cards.back: Yes. A standing pattern stores electric and magnetic energy while its signed Poynting flux can average to zero.

cards.front: What belongs in a distributed-field report?
cards.back: The source/boundary map, charge integral, field/potential profiles, interface signs, two energy integrals and numerical quadrature/refinement evidence.

cards.front: Why preserve interface and energy checks as separate evidence?
cards.back: A total energy value can hide a wrong local field or conductor sign; each original boundary and conservation identity constrains a different part of the model.

cards.front: How can a coupled-inductor report independently check an instantaneous result?
cards.back: Compare the matrix voltage equation with a direct energy derivative and retain all current/voltage references before integrating a transient.

cards.front: What verifies a transient source-work calculation?
cards.back: Integrate signed source input and nonnegative resistor loss and compare their difference with stored-energy change, alongside original voltage residuals and refinement.

cards.front: Which source-boundary evidence should a wave report retain?
cards.back: Field continuity/jump signs, retarded time, both outward normals and source-work versus emitted-flux cycle integrals under the declared model.

cards.front: Why compute cycle averages from the full incident/reflected fields?
cards.back: Their coherent cross terms and boundary signs determine standing energy and flux; adding traveling-wave magnitudes alone cannot verify those claims.

cards.front: What does a cumulative boundary report retain beyond a final value?
cards.back: Original state/charge equations, signed energy inputs and losses, independent transient/refinement checks and explicit counterexamples to overbroad field or power claims.

cards.front: Why identify the mathematical object behind a physical claim?
cards.back: A value, derivative, integral, local state and time-average flux constrain different properties. Their supporting equations and boundaries must remain explicit.
